properties.rationale:
These 64 boundaries are held in the code, not in the design, and that is correct rather than missing. A contract is declared at the lowest level that actually defines it and higher levels answer by roll-up (`dec:idea-a-contract-is-declared-at-the-lowest-level-and-rolled-up`, accepted 2026-08-23 on Anthony's word) — so the absence of an interface between two modules of one subsystem is the rule being followed, not a hole in the record.

Measured, not asserted: at module altitude `seam_coverage` reads 72 couplings, 8 covered, 64 uncovered; lifted to subsystem it reads 11 couplings, 11 covered, 0 uncovered. Independently, all 64 pairs sit inside ONE crate with zero crossing a crate boundary, and 44 of the 55 files in reflow2-core carry `impl DesignGraph` — so the majority of these "couplings" are impl blocks of the same struct calling each other. Writing 64 interface contracts for them would document a struct's method calls as system boundaries.

THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS DELIBERATELY NARROW. It accepts this finding on THIS design; it does not change what the undeclared-seam detector reports anywhere else. Defaulting the detector to subsystem altitude was offered and declined, because a roll-up answering "covered" at subsystem level says nothing about a coupling covered by no contract at ANY level — the counter-argument Anthony recorded beside his own idea before he was asked to settle it.

WHAT WOULD OVERTURN THIS: reflow2 splitting into separately-released crates. The moment one of these module pairs crosses a release boundary it becomes a real contract, and this reason stops holding for that pair. The review expiring when any of the 31 affected components change is the mechanism that should catch it.
